correctness.rationale: With unit total continuous-time jump rate per walker, the vacant-hub holding time is 1/k in expectation and its next state is A_(k-1). From A_k the three rates are k to A_(k-1), k/m to B_k, and (m-k)/m to B_(k+1); at k=m the last term is absent and at k=1 both one-walker states are absorbing. These give a_1=(3m-1)/(2(m+1)) and a_k-a_(k-1)=(2m+1)/((m+1)k)-1/(k+1), reproducing the formula, the gap, and the saturation equality of means. Clique thinning gives merger rates j(j-1)/m and the telescoping sum m²/(m+1). Comparison follows from H_m≤1+(m-2)/2+1/m for m≥2, strictly below m-1+1/m for m>2; m=1 is checked directly. The harmonic asymptotic has the stated constant and error. A newly written Fraction test checked all 144 reduced classes for 1≤m≤12 as well as the clique sum; the frozen source's separate full-state test is recorded evidence, not a replay or attestation.
residual_risks: Means only, with unit total rate per walker, not equal rate per edge or synchronous discrete-time jumps.
